newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rise in short session before Christmas.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rise in short session before Christmas.

text.p: Stocks rose Tuesday as investors scooped up big-name stocks and rushed off to celebrate Christmas.
The dollar also rose and bonds ended little changed in an abbreviated session before the holiday on Wednesday.

The Dow Jones industrial average rose 33.83 points to 6,522.85. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,295 to 921 on very light volume of 167 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The stock market closed early at 1 p.m. EST (1800GMT) and will be closed on Christmas Day.
"Santa is surprising us again. The traditional Christmas rally is at hand," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
"It's the last day for Christmas shopping and the last day of trading before Christmas. We have a holiday environment with much of the tax-selling apparently behind us."

The rally bodes well for Wall Street's prospects according to the old saying -- "If Santa should fail to call, bears could come to Broad and Wall," the streets that are the site of the New York Stock Exchange.

As for the Dow's action, David Kelly, senior economist with Primark Decision Economics, said, "It's not a sign of people rooting out value in smaller companies, it's just money looking for a safe home."
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was unchanged, leaving the yield at 6.59 percent.
In currency trading, the dollar climbed to its highest level against the Swiss franc in more than two years on worries about the weak economy in Switzerland.
The dollar surged early in New York to 1.3465 Swiss francs, the highest level since September 1994. The dollar settled at 1.3455 francs, up from 1.3373 francs late Monday. The dollar
rose to 1.5565 German marks and 114.47 Japanese yen from 1.5545 marks and 114.08 yen late Monday.
Financial markets in the United States and Europe will be closed for Christmas Day. Trading reopens in France and the United States on Thursday and in other major European markets Friday.
On commodities markets, grain and oil prices closed mostly higher in light trading during abbreviated trading sessions.
At the Chicago Board of Trade grain prices were led higher by a strong speculative rally in soybeans led by Refco Inc., a large professional trader, floor sources said.
Overseas, Tokyo's benchmark Nikkei average of 225 leading shares tumbled 528.75 points or 2.7 percent to 19,161.71, another 12-month low. London's FTSE 100 blue-chip index rose 5.3 points to 4,092.5.
